Indian IT stocks poised to beat global AI peers by most in decades

The latest survey of chief information officers globally showed stable growth in 2027. Software stocks are now the cheapest they have been since the pandemic year.

Chiranjivi Chakraborty ,  Samie Modak  and  Alex Gabriel Simon Thattil

16 October, 2026 02:05 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

The HCL Technologies Ltd. booth at the Semicon India expo in New Delhi, India. Photo: Prakash Singh/Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

India’s information-technology stocks are poised to beat their global semiconductor rivals by the most in two decades this week, with analysts saying the sector is set to keep outperforming as the artificial-intelligence rally unwinds.

An index of India’s biggest software exporters surged over 10% week, while a MSCI gauge of global chip stocks tumbled 7.4%, putting the former on course for the biggest weekly outperformance since 2004. AI shares have tumbled in recent days as slowing revenue growth, concerns about infrastructure financing, and renewed fears of rate hikes have fueled concerns that the companies are overvalued.

“If the correction in semiconductors gains momentum, as it has this week, foreign investors will start looking at Indian IT stocks,” said Rajat Agarwal, an Asia strategist at Societe Generale SA in Bengaluru. “We could probably see the end of de-rating in these companies, which itself should bring stability.”

Show Full Article

There have also been some positive signs for IT shares. HCL Technologies Ltd. raised its full-year sales growth guidance this week, while Ireland-based Accenture Plc said it expects to increase revenue growth and profit margins through 2029.

India’s largest IT firms were swept up in a global selloff in software stocks earlier this year, as some investors feared that AI could disrupt their business models. Slowing revenue growth amid geopolitical concerns and rising client demand for lower prices also sapped investor sentiment.

On Friday, Nifty IT Index gained as much as 3% in early trading, extending an advance to the fourth day. The gauge has climbed over 22% from its July low, but it’s still down about 17% this year, putting it on track for its worst annual performance since 2022.

“Although valuations appear reasonable now, on a relative and absolute basis, the sector lacks near-term catalysts,” Morgan Stanley analysts led by Gaurav Rateria wrote in a note this week.

The latest survey of chief information officers globally showed stable growth in 2027, and together with Accenture’s earnings, that points to steady-to-decelerating revenue growth for Indian IT firms, the Morgan Stanley analysts said.

Still, software stocks are now the cheapest they have been since the pandemic year. Stocks in the Nifty IT Index trade at less than 17 times their one-year forward earnings, nearly two standard deviations below the five-year average.

The sector’s bellwether, Infosys Ltd., is due to release its second-quarter earnings and commentary on Oct. 23, with the Bengaluru-based firm expected to report revenue growth of just 1.8%.

Looking ahead, at least some in the market see a longer rebound.

“An analysis of major innovations in the past indicates that while early stages of transition did witness a slowdown, it was immediately followed by a longer period of growth,” said Sumanta Khan, fund manager for equity at Edelweiss Asset Management Ltd.

Finance Minister Sitharaman says trade barriers the ‘biggest hurdle’ in India-China ties

Speaking with the Atlantic Council on the sidelines of the International Monetary Fund meeting in Bangkok, she called out China for denying market access to India’s goods.

Srinidhi Ragavendran  and  Ruchi Bhatia

16 October, 2026 01:14 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Nirmala Sitharaman during the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Thailand on Oct. 15. Photographer: Sirachai Arunrugstichai/Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

India faces growing trade imbalances with China as Beijing’s non-tariff barriers continue to restrict access for Indian products, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Friday.

“With China, I think our trade balance is against us, and it is growing exponentially,” Sitharaman said on the sidelines of the International Monetary Fund meeting in Bangkok, speaking with the Atlantic Council. “China uses non-tariff barriers unhesitatingly” and that is “the biggest hurdle in the in the trade between India and China.”

Sitharaman cited phytosanitary rules — restrictions intended to protect against plant pests and diseases — among the barriers facing Indian exporters. She called out China for denying market access to India’s goods that have “immense” potential in the mainland, including generic drugs, beef and vegetables.

Show Full Article

India-China ties plunged into a deep freeze in 2020 after a deadly border clash, triggering years of diplomatic distrust and restrictions on Chinese investments and business ties. Relations have gradually improved since then, with New Delhi and Beijing taking steps to ease border tensions and restore high-level engagement. India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping have also renewed efforts to stabilize ties.

India’s trade deficit with China has crossed $100 billion so far this year. Yet, Sitharaman said, India has not sought to retaliate with any non-tariff barriers or countervailing duties. Sitharaman’s comments come after External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said earlier this week that India isn’t “getting a level playing field in China.”

Beyond India-China ties, Sitharaman also took aim at India’s trade relationship with southeast Asian nations, describing existing trade agreements as “very skewed” against India.

While New Delhi intends to maintain its trade agreement with the ASEAN bloc, the terms would need to be refashioned, she said.

India remains the world’s fastest-growing major economy, supported by strong consumption and investment. Sitharaman, however, flagged the country’s dependence on imported crude oil and fertilizers as a key vulnerability. The bill for those essential imports is “big and growing,” she said, adding to the flow of foreign exchange out of the country.

The rupee has come under sustained pressure this year as surging oil prices swell India’s import bill, while foreign capital outflows and high US yields add to demand for dollars. The Reserve Bank of India has stepped up its defense of the currency, selling dollars and introducing measures including a special facility to meet state-owned oil companies’ foreign-exchange needs and tighter rules on currency derivatives. Those steps have helped the rupee recover from near-record lows, though the underlying pressures remain.

Reliance responds to Musk’s claims on Starlink’s India entry, says it ‘welcomes competition’

The response comes days after SpaceX CEO Elon Musk targeted the Indian conglomerate, alleging that vested interests were blocking Starlink's entry into India.

ANI

16 October, 2026 11:07 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

A Jio Platforms Ltd. logo at a news conference ahead of the company's listing ceremony at Reliance Corporate Park in Mumbai, India. Photo: Indranil Aditya for Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: Reliance Industries issued a statement on Friday that it welcomes competition in India’s satellite communications space, including Elon Musk’s Starlink, while emphasizing that every participant in the sector must adhere to the rule of law and existing national regulations.

“In light of recent remarks about Reliance and the Indian market, we wish to place the facts on record. Like every Indian enterprise, Reliance has grown in an India that welcomes investment and innovation, homegrown or international, that improve the lives of the people. That openness rests on the rule of law. As the Government of India has stated, it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign. Jio’s own satellite services await clearances,” the statements published on X said.

“At Reliance, we have never feared competition. We see it as the truest test of who serves the customer best. Jio itself entered India’s crowded telecom market in 2016 as the newest player, with not a single customer. In just ten years, Jio has earned the trust of over 530 million customers and given Indians some of the best digital infrastructure and most affordable data in the world. We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink. Every player, Jio included, must serve the people of India and abide by the laws and policies of the land,” the statement added.

The response from Reliance came after SpaceX Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk targeted the Indian conglomerate, alleging that vested interests were blocking Starlink’s entry into the sphere.

Show Full Article

In a post on X, Musk had said, “The ridiculous arguments by Ambani’s army of Internet shills make no sense. On the one hand, they say Starlink couldn’t possibly compete with the amazing low prices offered by Ambani’s de facto monopoly in India and then, in the same breath, they essentially claim that Starlink would be too strong of a competitor! This is absurd hypocrisy and hyperbole.”

He claimed that greater competition could reduce the profits of existing players but said it would not necessarily threaten their business.

“The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does. Ambani’s profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business,” he wrote.

Musk had earlier alleged monopolistic practices in the Indian telecommunications landscape and questioned regulatory barriers faced by Starlink’s commercial rollout.

“Dear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?” Musk posted.

Meanwhile, Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said that there was no question of allowing any monopoly in satellite communications and that three parties are in line for final approval for commercial licences.

Scindia said India is close to a final decision on the pricing framework for satellite communication services, and that all licensed operators, including Starlink, must meet security requirements before commercial operations begin.

Entertainment

Netflix replaces content chief to bolster search for hits

The new CCO, Peter Rice previously served as chairman of general entertainment at Walt Disney Co., and as president of 21st Century Fox.

Dawn Chmielewski  and  Thomas Buckley

16 October, 2026 10:18 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Peter Rice Photographer: Arturo Holmes/Getty Images

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

Netflix Inc. is replacing its chief creative officer with a veteran TV and film executive, Peter Rice, accelerating efforts to reinvigorate growth and reverse a slowdown in viewers and revenue at the streaming giant.

Rice previously served as chairman of general entertainment at Walt Disney Co., and, before that, as president of 21st Century Fox. He assumes the new role on Oct. 26, with a broad mandate, overseeing scripted and unscripted series, film and live events across all regions. Rice replaces Bela Bajaria, who had worked at Netflix for 10 years and come to be the public face of the company’s content strategy.

Peter Rice Photographer: Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images/Bloomberg The executive shakeup, coupled with Wednesday’s layoffs of some 1,000 workers or 6% of the workforce, are a sign that the streaming industry leader is trying to reinvent itself after seeing its audience growth slow and stock price tumble.

Show Full Article

The service has grown to more than 325 million subscribers globally. But it has evolved from a producer of “prestige TV” shows like House of Cards and The Crown to a broader entertainment source, competing with everything from sports channels to YouTube videos, and doing so on a global basis.

Bela Bajaria Photographer: Kyle Grillot/Bloomberg In moving Rice into the role, Netflix’s senior leadership see an opportunity to install an executive with deep relationships to Hollywood talent and experience running a broad portfolio of channels and streaming services. At Fox and later at Disney, he supervised a TV lineup that included hits from The Simpsons to Modern Family.

Recent Netflix shows have seen their audiences decline in their second seasons. The service saw its Emmy Awards wins fall to a 10-year low in 2026. The stock, which has lost about 23% of its value this year, fell 1.1% in extended trading.

Netflix co-Chief Executive Officer Ted Sarandos, speaking at the Bloomberg Screentime conference in Los Angeles last month, acknowledged that the company isn’t growing as fast as he would like. While the company has been expanding into live sports and podcasts, the vast majority of Netflix’s roughly $20 billion programming budget goes to films, TV shows and video games.

“Peter is one of the most effective at-scale operators in the entertainment industry,” Sarandos said in a statement Thursday. “He understands what makes stories resonate, and he’s spent his career helping talent do the best work of their lives.”

Netflix Growth is Slowing | Competition from YouTube and a lack of big titles is weighing on the streamer. Bajaria was credited with broadening Netflix’s entertainment offerings by expanding its unscripted portfolio and striking a deal with the TKO Group Holdings Inc.to bring the WWE’s weekly wrestling show, Raw, to the streaming service. She memorably described the ideal Netflix program as a “gourmet cheeseburger” — something that combines quality and broad appeal.

“Losing Bela Bajaria is a big change, but Peter Rice is very well regarded in the industry,” Alicia Reese, an analyst at Wedbush Securities, said by email. “To us, this is a step forward, or at least a shift in direction.”

Netflix’s shift from a streaming service to a platform with more varied content fits Rice’s experience well, Reese said. His experience consolidating Fox’s entertainment assets with Disney suggests that Netflix may look at other acquisitions, such as NBCUniversal when it becomes available, after being outbid by Skydance Corp. for Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. earlier this year.
